bodyHtml:
Use this guide to decide whether cheerio belongs on your shortlist: start with its stated purpose, then check setup, activity signals, maintenance clues, and adoption risks.

What is cheerio?

The fast, flexible & elegant library for parsing and manipulating HTML and XML.

Evidence: npmjs.com

Who should consider it?

This guide is most relevant to frontend developers evaluating tools in the JavaScript/TypeScript ecosystem. The source associates the project with htmlparser, jquery, selector, scraper. Treat it as a starting point for a shortlist, then compare the official documentation with your own requirements.

Evidence: npmjs.com

Why is it getting attention?

The package appeared in this feed because its recorded weekly npm activity made it notable at collection time. Download totals include automated requests and do not equal unique users, satisfaction, or product quality.

At collection time, the official source recorded latest version 1.2.0, and that version published on 2026-01-23.

Evidence: registry.npmjs.org

How to evaluate it

Start with the official package documentation and current release notes. Before adding cheerio to a project, check runtime compatibility, dependency impact, license terms, and whether the package's documented purpose matches your use case.

Treat weekly registry downloads as request volume, not unique users or GitHub star growth. Check current versions, dependencies, provenance, and compatibility before adoption.

Evidence: npmjs.com, cheerio.js.org, registry.npmjs.org, github.com

Bottom line

cheerio has enough public source information to warrant a closer look, but the available activity signals are not a recommendation. The useful next step is to verify fit against the official documentation and test the project for your own constraints.
